title: API Documentation
description: Learn how to write and generate clear API documentation so other developers can discover, understand, and integrate with your endpoints without reading your source code.

data.text: Good API documentation is not a nice-to-have. It is the contract between your backend and every client that consumes it. When documentation is missing or stale, developers guess, copy old code, or waste time in Slack asking for examples.

OpenAPI is a standard format for describing REST APIs. It defines endpoints, request parameters, response shapes, and authentication in a JSON or YAML file. Tools can then render it as a webpage, generate client SDKs, or validate requests against it.

items: YAML or JSON file that describes every endpoint
Machine-readable so tools can generate docs, clients, and tests
Supports examples, schemas, and authentication details
Works with Swagger UI, Redoc, and Stoplight

data.text: You do not need a huge file to get value. A minimal OpenAPI document with one endpoint already gives consumers request bodies, response codes, and data types they can rely on.

data.title: Minimal OpenAPI document for a posts endpoint
data.code:
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Posts API
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /api/posts:
    get:
      summary: List posts
      responses:
        "200":
          description: A list of posts
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  posts:
                    type: array
                    items:
                      $ref: "#/components/schemas/Post"
    post:
      summary: Create a post
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/CreatePostInput"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Post created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Post"
components:
  schemas:
    Post:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
        title:
          type: string
        content:
          type: string
    CreatePostInput:
      type: object
      required:
        - title
        - content
      properties:
        title:
          type: string
          maxLength: 200
        content:
          type: string

data.text: Hand-maintained OpenAPI files drift quickly. A better approach is to generate them from your existing validation schemas or route definitions. Libraries like `next-openapi` or `@asteasolutions/zod-to-openapi` bridge Zod schemas into OpenAPI components.

data.title: Generating OpenAPI schema from Zod
Keep Docs Close to Code
data.text: Generate your OpenAPI file as part of your build or dev script. If docs live in a separate repo or wiki, they will fall out of sync. Automated generation is the only reliable way to keep them fresh.

Every endpoint should explain what it does, what the client must send, and what the client will receive. Include examples, error codes, and authentication requirements so developers can integrate without asking your team.

items: Required and optional parameters with types
All possible status codes and their meanings

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: Use OpenAPI to describe endpoints in a standard, toolable format
Generate docs from code instead of maintaining them by hand
Include request bodies, responses, errors, and auth details
Publish docs where consumers can find them without reading source
